title: Why Saving Feels Harder Than Spending
idea: A girl is given the same coin every week: spend it now or wait a week for two. The film follows her choices against a friend who waits, to show present bias (invented, no advice). From the 2026-11-15 research: top money keyword by opportunity.

cast.name: Lily
cast.look: girl, ponytail, red jumper, a small coin purse

cast.name: Grandpa
cast.look: old man, bald, white moustache, green cardigan

cast.name: Sam
cast.look: her friend, short hair, blue dungarees, a glass jar

scenes.title: One coin
scenes.place: Grandpa's front porch on a Saturday morning, a wooden step and a flower pot

lines.t: Every Saturday, Grandpa gave Lily one coin.
Spend it now, or wait a week and get two.

scenes.title: The candy
scenes.place: the corner shop across the street, a big jar of bright candy on the counter

lines.t: The candy was right there. Two coins were a whole week away.

scenes.title: Sam's jar
scenes.place: the same porch in summer, Sam shaking a jar full of coins

lines.t: Sam waited. By summer, Sam had a whole jar.
Same coins. Why is waiting so hard?

scenes.title: Present bias
scenes.place: Grandpa's shed, a chalkboard with today and next week drawn as two piles

lines.t: It's called present bias. Your brain shrinks anything later.
Picture next week's two coins, and today's one looks small.
So, one coin today, or two next week?
